revision_notes: Light check surfaced substantive, on-topic legal sources, so this was escalated from the fast path. Fetched DLA Piper's Data Protection Laws of the World (Cape Verde, updated Jan 2025) and a compliance summary (ConsentStack), both describing Law 133/V/2001 (as amended by Law 41/VIII/2013 and Law 121/IX/2021), which regulates cross-border transfer of personal data via an adequacy/consent test similar to GDPR but does not require in-country storage. A payments-industry compliance guide (PayAtlas, Jan 2026) explicitly states 'there are no strict data localisation mandates' for Cape Verde, though critical financial data must be adequately protected under Banco de Cabo Verde guidelines. No sector-specific (telecoms, financial, government) storage mandate was found. Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (No data localisation requirements).
revised_comments: Cape Verde has no general legal or regulatory requirement mandating that personal, government, financial or critical infrastructure data be stored within national borders. Its data protection regime, established by Law 133/V/2001 as amended by Law 41/VIII/2013 and Law 121/IX/2021, is modelled closely on the EU GDPR and instead governs cross-border transfers through an adequacy assessment or explicit consent requirement, with extraterritorial scope covering foreign controllers processing Cape Verdean residents' data. The Comissão Nacional de Protecção de Dados (CNPD) oversees compliance and authorises transfers. Financial-sector data handled by payment service providers must be adequately protected under Banco de Cabo Verde guidelines, but this falls short of a data residency mandate.
